Surah An-Najm (The Star)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the star﴾: He swears by the Pleiades (al-Thurayya), or by the category of stars in general.

﴿When it sets﴾: when it goes down (gharaba), or when it is scattered on the Day of Resurrection. And the answer to the oath is:

ما ضَلَّ (He has not strayed) — from the straight course of truth.

صاحِبُكُمْ (your companion) — that is, Muhammad (ﷺ). The address is to the Quraysh.

وَما غَوى (nor has he gone astray) — in following falsehood. It was said: ḍalāl (ضلال) is the opposite of guidance (hudā), and ghayy (غي) is the opposite of rectitude (rushd). That is, he is guided and rightly guided, and it is not as you claim in attributing to him straying and error.

﴿Wa ma yanṭiqu ʿani l-hawā﴾ ﴿In huwa illā waḥyun yūḥā﴾: "Nor does he speak from (his own) desire. It is only a revelation that is revealed." The verse means that what has come to you of the Qur'an through him is not a speech issuing from his own desire and opinion; rather, it is a revelation from Allah, revealed to him. Those who do not regard ijtihad (independent legal reasoning) as permissible for the prophets, peace be upon them, cite this verse as evidence. It is answered that when Allah (exalted is He) permits them to exercise ijtihad and confirms them in it, that becomes like revelation, and not speech from desire.

﴿Wa ma yanṭiqu ʿani l-hawā﴾ ﴿In huwa illā waḥyun yūḥā﴾: "Nor does he speak from (his own) desire. It is only a revelation that is revealed." The verse means that what has come to you of the Qur'an through him is not a speech issuing from his own desire and opinion; rather, it is a revelation from Allah, revealed to him. Those who do not regard ijtihad (independent legal reasoning) as permissible for the prophets, peace be upon them, cite this verse as evidence. It is answered that when Allah (exalted is He) permits them to exercise ijtihad and confirms them in it, that becomes like revelation, and not speech from desire.

﴿He taught him﴾: he taught Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Mighty in power﴾: an angel mighty in his powers. The construction (idafa) here is not a true one, since it is the idafa of the attributive adjective (al-sifa al-mushabbaha) to its agent. The one meant, according to the majority (al-Jumhur), is Jibril (peace be upon him). Among his strength is that he uprooted the cities of the people of Lut from the black water, carried them on his wing, raised them up to the sky, then overturned them, and he cried out a single cry to Thamud, so they became lifeless in their homes.

(p-390) ﴿Dhu mirrah﴾ (possessor of strength): one with a handsome appearance. Related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father:

﴿Fastawa﴾ (he stood firm/appeared): he stood upright in his true, original form, not in the form in which he used to appear whenever he descended with the revelation. He would descend in the form of Dihyah (al-Kalbi). That was because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) loved to see him in the form in which he had been created, so he appeared to him on the highest horizon, which is the horizon of the sun, and he filled the horizon. It has also been said: none of the prophets (peace be upon them) saw him in his true form except Muhammad (ﷺ), twice: once on the earth and once in the heavens.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 7:

﴿And he﴾, i.e., Jibril (peace be upon him), ﴿was on the highest horizon﴾, the rising-place of the sun.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 8:

﴿Then he drew near﴾, Jibril, to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ),

﴿and came down, and was suspended﴾, he increased in nearness, and "al-tadalli" (descending close to a thing, i.e. coming down near to something) is the descent close to a thing.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 9:

﴿So he was at a distance of two bow-lengths﴾, the measure of two Arabic bows. Measurement has been expressed by means of the bow (qaws), the spear (rumh), the whip (sawt), the forearm (dhira'), and the fathom (ba'). From this is the saying: "There is no prayer until the sun rises the measure of two spears (rumhayn)." And in the hadith: "The distance of the bow of one of you in Paradise (laqab qaws) and the place of his whip (qadd) is better than the world and everything in it." And "al-qadd" means the whip. Its implied meaning is: "So the measure of the distance of his nearness was like the distance of two bow-lengths," so these added words (mudafat) have been omitted.

﴿Or nearer﴾, meaning: according to your estimation. This is like His saying: ﴿or they increase﴾ [al-Saffat: 147]. This is because they were addressed in their own language and according to the measure of their understanding, and they say: "This is the measure of two spears, or less." It was also said: "Rather, nearer (adna)."

﴿So He revealed﴾, Jibril (peace be upon him),

﴿to His servant﴾, to the servant of Allah. Although no name has been mentioned, it is understood, because there is no ambiguity, as in His saying: ﴿not a creature upon its back﴾ [Fatir: 45]. ﴿What He revealed﴾ is an exaltation of the revelation that was revealed to him. It has been said: "It was revealed to him that Paradise is forbidden to the prophets until you enter it, and forbidden to the nations until your nation enters it."

Ma kadhaba al-fu'ad (the heart) — the heart of Muhammad — ma ra'a. What he saw with his eyes of the form of Jibril (peace be upon him): that is, his heart did not say, when it saw him, "I do not know you." Had it said that, it would have been lying, because it recognised him; that is, he saw him with his eye and recognised him with his heart, and did not doubt that what he saw was true. (p-391) It is also said: the one seen is God, exalted is He; he saw Him with the eye of his head, and it is said with his heart.

Qur'anic quotations go in ﴿ ﴾ with plain meaning inside.

"Will you then dispute with him" (afa-tumārūnahu): i.e., will you then argue with him? From al-mirā' (mira', disputation), which is argument. Its derivation is from "maryu al-nāqah" (milking the she-camel, i.e., stroking her udder to draw out milk), as though each of the two disputants draws out what is in the other's possession. "Afa-tamrūnahu" (will you then contend with him or overcome him in dispute?) is read by Ḥamzah, ʿAlī, Khalaf and Yaʿqūb. "Will you then overcome him in disputation?!" is from "māraytuhu fa-maraytuhu" (I disputed with him and I prevailed over him). Because of the meaning of overpowering contained in it, He said: ﴿over what he sees﴾, so it takes "ʿalā" (over), just as you say "ghalabtuhu ʿalā kadhā" (I overcame him in such-and-such). It is also said: "afa-tamrūnahu" means: will you then deny him? One says "maraytuhu ḥaqqahu" (I denied him his right) when you deny it to him, and its construction with "ʿalā" is not valid except according to the view of taḍmīn (the principle that a verb is construed as carrying the sense of another verb).

﴿And he certainly saw him﴾: Muhammad (ﷺ) saw Jibril, peace be upon them both,

﴿another descent﴾, another time, from "al-nuzul" (descending). The word *nazlah* is put in the accusative in the manner of an adverb of time (*zarf*, an adverbial noun of time or place), in the sense of "مَرَّةً" (*marratan*, "once"). This is because the pattern *fa'lah* is a noun for a single occurrence of the verb (*al-fi'l*, the action), so it has the same status as the adverb. The meaning is: Jibril, peace be upon him, descended to him another descent in his own form, and so he saw him in that form. That was on the night of the Mi'raj (the Ascension).

"near the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary" (﴿عِنْدَ سِدْرَةِ المُنْتَهى﴾)? Translating the passage:

The majority of scholars hold that it is a lote-tree (sidrah, nabq) in the seventh heaven, to the right of the Throne (al-'Arsh). As for "al-Muntaha" (the Utmost Boundary), it means "the place of ending" (mawdi' al-intiha'), or it is "the ending" (al-intiha') itself, as if it lies at the furthest end and last extremity of Paradise. It has also been said: no one has passed beyond it, and to it the knowledge of the angels and others ends, and no one knows what lies beyond it. It has also been said: the souls of the martyrs ascend to it.

ﷻ﴿Indeed, near it is the Garden of Refuge﴾. That is: the Garden to which the righteous (al-muttaqun) will go. And it was said: it is the Garden to which the spirits of the martyrs (al-shuhada') retreat.

ﷺ

﴿When there covered the lote-tree that which covered it﴾ — i.e., he saw it: "when there covered the lote-tree that which covered it." This is an expression of magnification and of amplifying what covers it. By this expression it is known that what covers it of the creatures — which indicate the greatness of Allah (Exalted is He) and His majesty — are things that description cannot encompass. It has been said: it is covered by a vast multitude of angels, worshipping Allah (Exalted is He) in its presence. And it has been said: it is covered by butterflies of gold.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 17:

﴿His sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress.﴾ The sight of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not turn away from seeing the wonders which he was made to pass by and was empowered to see.

﴿Nor did it transgress.﴾ That is, it did not go beyond what it was commanded to see.

(p-392) ﴿Indeed he saw﴾, "By Allah, he indeed saw"

﴿of the greatest signs of his Lord﴾: the signs which are greatest and most magnificent. He means: when he was raised up to the heavens, and was shown the wonders of the malakut (the unseen dominion of God).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on Surah 53, verses 19–20:

﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza,﴾ ﴿and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ Meaning: tell us about these things that you worship besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Do they possess the power and greatness with which the Lord of Might is described?! "Al-Lat," "al-Uzza," and "Manat" are idols belonging to them, and they are feminine. Al-Lat belonged to the Thaqif, at al-Ta'if. It is said that Quraysh worshipped it at Nakhla. It is on the pattern *fa'lah*, from *lawa* (to turn or wind around), because they used to circle around it and remain in devotion (*ya'kufun*) for worship. Al-Uzza belonged to Ghatafan. It was a *samurah* (acacia tree). Its root is the feminine of *al-A'azz* (the most mighty). Khalid ibn al-Walid cut it down. Manat was a rock belonging to Hudhayl and Khuza'a. It is said it belonged to the Thaqif. It is likely that it was named Manat because the blood of the sacrificial animals was poured out (*tuma*) there, meaning shed. "Wa-Manah" (as read by Ibn Kathir in some transmissions) is Meccan, on the pattern *maf'alah*, from *al-nau'* (the rain-star), as though they sought rain (*yastamtirun*) through the rain-stars there, seeking blessing through it.

﴿The other﴾: this is an adjective of disparagement, meaning the one that comes later, the lowly in rank, like His saying: ﴿Its latter ones will say to its former ones﴾ [al-A'raf: 38], meaning their followers to their leaders and nobles. It is also possible that the precedence and priority among them belonged to al-Lat and al-Uzza. They used to say that the angels and these idols are the daughters of Allah. They would worship them and claim that they were their intercessors with Allah, along with their burying of daughters and their aversion to them. So it was said to them:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 21–22:

﴿Is it for you the male, and for Him the female?﴾ ﴿That indeed would be an unjust division!﴾ Meaning: "Your making for Allah the daughters, and for you the sons, is an unjust division (qisma ḍīzā), that is, oppressive (jā'ira), from "ḍāzahu, yaḍīzuhu" (ḍāzahu, yaḍīzuhu), when he wronged him (idhā aḍāmahu). And "ḍīzā" is of the pattern "fu'lā", since there is no "fi'lā" pattern among adjectives (al-nu'ūt), so the ḍād was given a kasra because of the yā', just as it is said "bīḍ" (bīḍ), which is "būḍ", like "ḥumr" and "sūd", (and) "ḍi'zā", with a hamza, (is the reading) of Meccan (Makkī), from "ḍa'azahu", like "ḍāzahu".

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 21–22:

﴿Is it for you the male, and for Him the female?﴾ ﴿That indeed would be an unjust division!﴾ Meaning: "Your making for Allah the daughters, and for you the sons, is an unjust division (qisma ḍīzā), that is, oppressive (jā'ira), from "ḍāzahu, yaḍīzuhu" (ḍāzahu, yaḍīzuhu), when he wronged him (idhā aḍāmahu). And "ḍīzā" is of the pattern "fu'lā", since there is no "fi'lā" pattern among adjectives (al-nu'ūt), so the ḍād was given a kasra because of the yā', just as it is said "bīḍ" (bīḍ), which is "būḍ", like "ḥumr" and "sūd", (and) "ḍi'zā", with a hamza, (is the reading) of Meccan (Makkī), from "ḍa'azahu", like "ḍāzahu".

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 23:

﴿They are nothing but names﴾, that is, the idols,

﴿which you and your fathers have named, for which God has sent down no authority﴾. They have no reality beneath them in truth, namely named objects (musammayat), because you ascribe divinity (al-ilahiyyah) to that which is farthest from it and most incompatible with it.

﴿You have named them﴾, that is, you have named things by them. It is said: "sammaytuhu Zaydan" and "sammaytuhu bi-Zayd" (I named him Zayd).

﴿You and your fathers, [for which] God has sent down no authority﴾, that is, no proof (hujjah).

﴿They follow nothing but conjecture﴾, that is, nothing but the supposition that what they hold is true.

﴿And what their souls desire﴾, that is, what their souls crave.

﴿Yet guidance has already come to them from their Lord﴾, namely the Messenger and the Book, but they abandoned it and did not act upon it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 24:

﴿Or does man get whatever he wishes?﴾ This is "am" (or) that is "munqati'a" (disjunctive), and the meaning of the hamza (interrogative particle) in it is denial. That is: man—meaning the disbeliever—does not get whatever he wishes, such as the intercession of the idols, or [what he wishes from] the saying: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, surely I shall have the best with Him﴾ [Fussilat: 50]. It is also said: it is the wish of some of them that he (ﷺ) should be the Prophet.

﴿So to Allah belongs the Hereafter and the first [life]﴾. That is: He is their owner, and the judgment concerning both is His; He gives prophethood and intercession to whomever He wills and approves, not to whoever wishes for it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 26:

﴿And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession avails nothing, except after Allah has given permission to whomever He wills and is pleased with.﴾ He means that the matter of intercession is restricted. Even though the angels are close to Allah and numerous, if they all interceded together for anyone, their intercession would avail nothing at all and would not benefit, except when they intercede after Allah has granted them permission to intercede for whomever He wills to be interceded for and is pleased with, and whom He deems fit to be interceded for. How, then, could idols intercede with Him for their worshippers?!

Qur'anic quotations keep the markers. Translate.

﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter surely name the angels﴾ with the name of females, meaning: each one of them,

﴿the naming of females﴾, because when they say, "The angels are daughters of Allah," they have named each one of them a daughter, and this is the naming of females.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 28:

﴿And they have no knowledge of it.﴾ That is, of what they say. It is also read as "bihā" (with it), meaning: of the angels, or of the naming (al-tasmiyah).

﴿They follow nothing but conjecture (al-zann).﴾ This is the imitation (taqlid) of their forefathers.

﴿And indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth.﴾ That is: the truth, which is the reality of a thing and what it is in itself, is only known through knowledge (ʿilm) and certainty (tayaqqun), not through conjecture (zann) and mere supposition (tawahhum).

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 29:**

﴿So turn away from those who turn away from Our remembrance﴾: turn away from the one whom you see turning away from the remembrance of Allah, that is, the Qur'an [p. 394],

﴿and who desires nothing but the life of this world﴾.

That is: their choosing the worldly life and being content with it.

﴿That is the extent of their knowledge﴾, the limit of their knowledge.

﴿Indeed your Lord knows best who strays from His way, and He knows best who is guided﴾. That is: He knows best the one who goes astray and the one who is guided, and He will recompense both of them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 31:

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, that He may recompense those who have done evil according to what they have done﴾, by the punishment for what they did of evil, or on account of (bi-sabab) what they did of evil,

﴿and that He may recompense those who have done good with the best (al-husna)﴾, with the best reward (al-mathuba al-husna), which is Paradise, or on account of the good deeds (al-a'mal al-husna). The meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the world and arranged this dominion (malakut) only that He might recompense the doer of good among the accountable (mukallafin) and the doer of evil among them, since the King is fit to grant victory to His allies and to subdue His enemies.

﴿Alladhina﴾ (Those who). It is either a substitute (badal) or in the nominative position, by way of praise. That is, they are the ones who

﴿avoid major sins (kaba'ira) of wrongdoing﴾. That is, the major sins of wrongdoing. Because wrongdoing (ithm) is a genus that includes major and minor sins. "Al-kaba'ir" are the sins whose punishment is great. "Kabir" is read by Hamza and Ali, meaning the major kind of it.

﴿And the gross indecencies (fawahish)﴾: what is especially grave among the major sins. It is as if he said: "And especially the gross indecencies among them." It has been said: "Major sins" are those for which God has threatened the Fire, and "gross indecencies" are those for which a prescribed punishment (hadd) has been legislated.

﴿except for minor lapses (lamam)﴾. That is, the minor sins. The exception is disjunctive (istithna' munqati'), because it is not among the major sins or the gross indecencies. It is like a glance, a kiss, a touch, or a squeeze.

﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾, so He forgives whatever sins He wills, without repentance.

﴿He knows you best, when He brought you forth﴾, that is, your father (Adam),

﴿from the earth, and when you were embryos (ajinna)﴾, the plural of "janin" (fetus),

﴿in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim purity for yourselves (fa-la tuzakkuha anfusakum)﴾: do not attribute them to the purity of deeds, or the increase of good and acts of obedience, or to purity (zakah) and cleanness from disobedience. Do not praise them, but belittle them. For God knows the pure among you and the God-fearing, at the beginning and the end, before He brought you out from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, and before you came out from the wombs of your mothers. It has also been said: some people used to do good deeds and then say, "Our prayer, our fasting, and our pilgrimage," so this was revealed. This applies when it is done by way of self-admiration (ijab) or ostentation (riya'). It is not so when it is by way of acknowledging a blessing, for that is permissible, because joy in an act of obedience is itself obedience, and mentioning it is gratitude.

(p-٣٩٥)﴿He knows best who is God-fearing﴾. So they should be content with His knowledge instead of the knowledge of people, and with His reward instead of the praise of people.

Surah 53, verse 33:

﴿Have you seen the one who turned away?﴾ He turned away from faith.

﴿And he gave a little, and then held back.﴾ He cut off his giving and withheld. Its origin is "ikdaa' al-hafir" (the digger's hitting hard ground), which is when the digger meets a *kudya*, a hard obstacle like a rock, so he stops digging.

From Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): "It refers to one who disbelieved after having embraced Islam." It is also said: it was about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. He had followed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but some of the disbelievers reproached him and said to him: "You abandoned the religion of our forefathers and claimed that they are in the Fire?!" He said: "I feared the punishment of Allah." So (the disbeliever) guaranteed him that if he gave him some of his wealth and returned to his polytheism, he would bear the punishment of Allah on his behalf. He did so, and gave the one who had reproached him some of what he had guaranteed him, then he became stingy with it and withheld it.
﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees?﴾ So he knows that what he guaranteed of Allah's punishment is true?!

Surah al-Najm (53), verse 36 in the commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil):

﴿Or has he not been informed﴾, i.e., told,

﴿of what is in the scrolls of Musa﴾, i.e., the Torah.

﴿And Abraham﴾, that is: and in the scrolls of Abraham,

﴿who fulfilled﴾, that is: who completed and perfected, as in His saying: ﴿and he fulfilled them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124]. Its being unrestricted is so that it encompasses every fulfilment and every carrying-out. It is also read with the letters lightened (wafa), while the doubled form (waffa) denotes emphasis in fulfilment. From al-Hasan: "Allah did not command him with anything except that he fulfilled it." From ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib: "He covenanted not to ask any creature. When he was cast into the fire, Jibril said to him, 'Do you have any need?' He said, 'As for you, no.'" From the Prophet (ﷺ): "He fulfilled his deed every day with four rak'ahs at the beginning of the day, which is the Duha prayer." It is also narrated: "Shall I not inform you why Allah named His friend 'who fulfilled'? He used to say, when he woke in the morning and when he entered the evening: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ [al-Rum: 17], up to ﴿and when you dhuhr﴾ [al-Rum: 18]." It has also been said: "He fulfilled the arrows of Islam, which are thirty: ten in al-Tawbah, 'al-Ta'ibun...'; ten in al-Ahzab, 'Inna al-muslimin...'; and ten in al-Mu'minun, 'Qad aflaha al-mu'minun...'" (p-396) Then He informed of what is in the scrolls of Musa and Abraham, saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 38:

﴿That no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾. "Taziru" (تَزِرُ) is from "wazara, yaziru" (وَزَرَ، يَزِرُ), when one acquires a burden (wizr), which is sin (al-ithm). "An" (أنْ) is a lightened form of the heavy (mukhaffafa min al-thaqila), and the meaning is "that it is not the case that..." (أنَّهُ لا تَزِرُ). The pronoun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-sha'n). The position (maḥall) of "an" and what follows it is in the genitive (al-jarr), as a substitute (badal) for "what is in the scrolls of Musa" (ما في صُحُفِ مُوسى), or in the nominative (al-raf'), with the sense "it is that no bearer of burdens shall bear..." (هُوَ أنْ لا تَزِرُ). As if a speaker had said: "And what is in the scrolls of Musa and Ibrahim?" and it was answered: "That no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another" (أنْ لا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى), i.e., "that no soul shall bear the sin of another soul" (أنْ لا تَحْمِلُ نَفْسٌ ذَنْبَ نَفْسٍ).

Verse 39: ﴿And that there is not for man except what he strives for.﴾ Except his own striving. And this is also among what is in the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa. As for what is authentically reported in the traditions concerning charity on behalf of the deceased and pilgrimage on his behalf, it has been said: the striving of another, since it benefits him only when it is founded upon his own striving, which is that he be a believer, becomes as if it were his own striving, because it follows him and stands by his standing. Moreover, the striving of another does not benefit him if he performs it for his own self; but if he intends it on his behalf, then by the ruling of the Sharia it is like a deputy for him, and an agent standing in his place.
And that his effort will be seen (﴿وَأنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرى﴾). That is: he himself will see his effort on the Day of Resurrection in his scale.

ثُمَّ يُجْزَاهُ (then he shall be recompensed for it). Then the servant is recompensed for his striving. It is said: "Allah recompense him for his deed" (جَزَاهُ اللهُ عَمَلَهُ), and "recompense him for his deed" (جَزَاهُ عَلَى عَمَلِهِ), by omitting the preposition (al-jārr) and making the verb reach its object directly. It is also possible that the pronoun refers to the recompense (al-jazā'), and then he explains it with His saying: ﴿the fullest recompense﴾, or it is a substitute (badal) for it.

﴿And that to your Lord is the finality﴾. All of this is in the earlier scriptures. "Al-Muntaha" is a verbal noun (masdar) with the meaning of "al-intiha'" (the ending, the reaching of a limit), i.e., creation ends at Him and they return to Him, like His saying: ﴿And to Allah is the return﴾ [al-Nur: 42].

And that it is He who makes [people] laugh and weep. He created laughter and weeping. It is also said: He created joy and sorrow. And it is said: He makes the believers laugh in the Hereafter with gifts, and makes them weep in this world with calamities.

﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾. It is said: He causes the forefathers to die and gives life to the sons; or He causes death through disbelief and gives life through faith; or He causes death here and gives life there (in the Hereafter).
﴿From a drop of seminal fluid when it is emitted﴾, when it is poured forth into the womb. (p-٣٩٧) It is said: "manā" and "amnā".

The Qur'anic verse "And that unto your Lord is the final goal" is not what this line contains; the passage here is Q 53:47, which reads: ﴿And that it is He who brings about the second creation﴾.

Translation:

﴿And that it is upon Him that the second creation (al-nash'ah al-ukhra) depends﴾, meaning: the giving of life after death.

﴿And that it is He who enriches and grants possessions﴾. He gave *al-qinya* (lasting property, wealth one keeps for oneself), which is the wealth you have accumulated and resolved not to let out of your hand.

﴿And that He is the Lord of Sirius﴾. It is a star that rises after al-Jawza' (Orion), in the intensity of the heat. The Khuza'a used to worship it, so God made known that He is the Lord of this object of their worship.

﴿And that He destroyed the first ʿĀd﴾. They are the people of Hūd. As for the other ʿĀd, it is Iram. "ʿĀdan l-ūlā" (the reading of) the Medinan and the Basran, "ghayra sahl" (not easy), with idghām (assimilation) of the tanwīn (nunation) into the lām, dropping the hamza of "ūlā," and transferring its ḍamma to the lām of the definite article.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 51:

﴿And Thamud, He spared none of them.﴾ Hamzah and 'Asim read it as "wa-Thamuda" in the genitive-free form, while the rest (al-baqun) read "wa-Thamudan" (with fathah on the final letter). The latter is in the accusative, and it is coordinated (ma'tuf) on "'Adan" (and 'Ad), and it is not governed by "fa-ma abqa" (so he left none), because what comes after the fa' (fa' al-'ataf, the "then" particle) does not govern what comes before it. You do not say "Zaydan fa-darabtu" (Zayd, so I struck him) with Zayd as object of the verb after fa'. Likewise, what comes after a negation (nafy) does not govern what comes before it. The meaning is: "And He destroyed Thamud, so He left none of them."

And the people of Nuh before them, [He destroyed]; that is, He destroyed the people of Nuh (ʿalayhi al-salam),

from before, that is, from before ʿAd and Thamud,

"Indeed they were more unjust and more transgressing" than ʿAd and Thamud, because they used to beat him (ﷺ)... 

Correction to the above: the passage refers to Nuh (peace be upon him), not the Prophet (ﷺ). Corrected translation follows.

And the people of Nuh [He destroyed] before them, that is, He destroyed the people of Nuh,

from before, that is, from before ʿAd and Thamud,

"Indeed they were more unjust and more transgressing," than ʿAd and Thamud, because they used to beat him until there was no movement left in him, and they would drive people away from him, to the extent that they would warn their children not to listen to him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 53:

﴿And the overturned cities﴾, and the towns which were overturned with their people, i.e., turned upside down. They were the people of Lut (Lot). It is said: "afakahu, fa'tufika" (he overturned it, so it was overturned),

﴿He threw down﴾, i.e., He raised them up to the sky on the wing of Jibril (Gabriel), then He hurled them down to the earth, i.e., He made them fall. And "al-mu'tafikata" (the overturned cities) is in the accusative case, governed by "ahwa" (He threw down).

﴿Then He covered it﴾, He clothed it (with it).

﴿With that which covered it﴾: an expression of awe and magnification of what was poured down upon them of punishment and what was rained down upon them of stones of baked clay, piled one upon another.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord﴾, O you who are addressed,

﴿would you dispute﴾: do you doubt concerning what He has bestowed upon you of blessings, or what He has warded off from you of calamities?! Or do you doubt concerning which of the blessings of your Lord that point to His oneness and His lordship?!

(p-398) ﴿This is a warner﴾, i.e., Muhammad is a warner, ﴿from among the warners of old﴾, from among the earlier warners. He said "al-ūlā" (the former) in accordance with interpreting the group (al-jamāʿa) [as a collective noun]. Or [the meaning is]: "This Qur'an is a warner from among the former warnings" — i.e., a warning of the same kind as the earlier warnings with which those before you were warned.
﴿The approaching [Hour] has drawn near﴾, meaning the one described as drawing near in His saying: ﴿The Hour has drawn near﴾ [al-Qamar: 1].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 58:

﴿There is none to disclose it besides Allah.﴾ That is: there is no soul that discloses it, i.e., that makes clear when it will occur (qiyam), like His saying: ﴿None will reveal its time except Him﴾ [al-A'raf: 187]. Or: there is no soul able to disclose it when it befalls, except Allah (Exalted is He), though He does not disclose it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 53, verse 59:

﴿Do you then wonder at this discourse?﴾ That is, the Qur'an.

﴿Do you wonder﴾, in denial.

﴿And you laugh⦆, mocking;

﴿and do not weep⦆, out of humility.

﴿And you are sāmidūn (heedless)﴾: heedless, or playing, amusing yourselves. And when they heard the Qur'an, they would counter it with singing (ghinā'), in order to distract people from listening to it.

This is a short passage. The Qur'anic quotation is inside ﴿ ﴾, so it is translated plainly. Commentary: "أي" translates as "i.e." and "الآلهة" as "the deities".

﴿So prostrate to Allah and worship [Him]﴾ i.e., prostrate to Allah and worship Him, and do not worship the deities.
